entries.title: Full-slide gap protection
entries.summary: One documented protection family assigns the offensive line to slide toward gap responsibilities, commonly leaving a back responsible for the backside edge. SAGE should model protection as assignment structure, not merely offensive-line quality.

entries.title: Man/slide protection
entries.summary: Documented mixed protections assign one or more blockers man responsibility while other linemen slide to gap responsibilities; backs can own the gap created between those rules.

entries.title: Protection identification is multi-position work
entries.summary: Protection identification can involve quarterback, running backs and offensive line before the snap; SAGE should not attribute every pressure event solely to an offensive lineman.

entries.title: Separate assignment, technique and scheme weakness
entries.summary: A protection failure can arise from assignment error, technique failure, or a structural weakness against a particular pressure. Time-to-hurry/hit/sack adds context but does not by itself identify the cause.
fantasyImplications: Potentially separates persistent protection problems from QB/coverage-driven sacks and may improve QB/receiver matchup analysis after validation.

entries.title: Protection responsibility can alter fantasy route opportunity
entries.summary: When RBs or TEs absorb protection responsibility, route participation and target opportunity may change; SAGE should test protection burden together with pressure environment rather than infer receiving opportunity from snap share alone.
